# EarthBox

> EarthBox is a terrarium and 3D-printing studio in Kandivali, Mumbai 400101, India. It makes closed terrariums ("Elemental Boxes"), 3D-printed planters, moss poles and plant accessories (live plant packets are coming soon), and offers Care: refill kits and plant-care visits. Delivery within Mumbai. Orders and questions: WhatsApp +91 81048 11584 or aayush.lilani@gmail.com.

Prices are in Indian rupees. 3D-printed pieces are made to order (about 1 week). Pieces marked "Coming soon" can't be ordered yet.

## Pages
- [Catalogue](https://www.earthbox.in/products): every piece, with prices
- [Care](https://www.earthbox.in/care): refill kits and visit plans for homes in Mumbai; quotes for offices, cafés and hotels
- [About](https://www.earthbox.in/about): the studio and its founder, Aayush Lilani
- [Journal](https://www.earthbox.in/blog): guides to terrarium care and plants in Mumbai

## Journal
- [The Water Cycle Inside a Closed Terrarium](https://www.earthbox.in/blog/closed-terrarium-water-cycle): A closed terrarium creates a self-sustaining water cycle: plants release moisture through transpiration, water condenses on the glass walls, and droplets return to the soil. This cycle continues indefinitely without adding water.
- [How to Rescue an Overwatered Terrarium](https://www.earthbox.in/blog/rescue-overwatered-terrarium): Remove the lid for 24-48 hours to let excess moisture evaporate. Wipe condensation from glass daily. If mold appears, remove affected plants and soil, treat with diluted hydrogen peroxide, and reduce watering.
- [Open vs Closed Terrariums: Which is Right for You?](https://www.earthbox.in/blog/open-vs-closed-terrariums): Closed terrariums are sealed glass containers that create self-sustaining humid environments for tropical plants like ferns and moss. Open terrariums have no lid, suit succulents and cacti that prefer dry conditions, and require regular watering.
- [The First 30 Days: Terrarium Settling Guide](https://www.earthbox.in/blog/first-30-days-terrarium): New terrariums need 2-4 weeks to stabilize. Plants may droop initially as they adjust to humidity levels. Some leaf yellowing is normal. Avoid opening the lid frequently—let the ecosystem find its balance.
- [Why We 3D Print Our Planters: A Design Decision](https://www.earthbox.in/blog/why-we-3d-print-planters): 3D printing enables precise drainage systems, custom geometries, and rapid iteration. Each piece can be unique. Unlike injection molding, there is no minimum order—we can produce one perfect piece at a time.
- [PLA vs ABS for Plant Accessories: Material Guide](https://www.earthbox.in/blog/pla-vs-abs-plant-accessories): PETG suits most indoor planters: it resists moisture and prints cleanly. ABS handles more heat, which suits sunny windows, and ASA resists UV, which suits balconies. PLA absorbs moisture and softens in heat, so it is a poor choice for long-term planters.
- [Designing Drainage: How We Engineer Our Vessels](https://www.earthbox.in/blog/designing-drainage): We use parametric design to create drainage channels that guide water to exit points while retaining enough moisture. Raised internal feet keep roots above standing water. Each design is tested with real plants before production.
- [The Anatomy of an EarthBox Cradle](https://www.earthbox.in/blog/anatomy-earthbox-cradle): The cradle uses a parabolic curve that distributes weight evenly while creating visual lightness. The 3mm wall thickness provides strength without bulk. Integrated cable channels allow for hanging without visible hardware.
- [Monsoon Terrarium Care: Mumbai Edition](https://www.earthbox.in/blog/monsoon-terrarium-care-mumbai): During monsoon, ambient humidity rises to 90%+. Open closed terrariums for 2-3 hours daily to prevent oversaturation. Move terrariums away from windows to avoid temperature swings. Watch for mold—it thrives in monsoon conditions.
- [5 Native Indian Plants Perfect for Terrariums](https://www.earthbox.in/blog/native-indian-terrarium-plants): Native spikemosses (Selaginella), Peperomia tetraphylla from the Western Ghats, maidenhair ferns (Adiantum), local mosses and brake ferns (Pteris) all suit terrarium conditions. Pilea cadierei and Ficus pumila are popular here too, but they are not native.
- [Surviving Mumbai Summers: Indoor Plant Guide](https://www.earthbox.in/blog/mumbai-summer-indoor-plants): Snake plants, ZZ plants, pothos, and rubber plants handle Mumbai's 35-40°C summers. Avoid delicate ferns and calatheas during peak heat. Keep plants away from direct afternoon sun and increase watering frequency.
- [Where to Find Terrarium Supplies in Mumbai](https://www.earthbox.in/blog/terrarium-supplies-mumbai): Dadar flower market for plants and moss. Crawford Market for glass containers. Matunga and Versova nurseries for specialty soil. Online plant nurseries also deliver supplies to Mumbai.
- [Quiet Objects: The EarthBox Design Manifesto](https://www.earthbox.in/blog/quiet-objects-manifesto): We design quiet objects—pieces that do not demand attention but reward close looking. Every curve has a reason. Every material is chosen for how it ages. We create objects meant to be kept, not replaced.
- [Why We Release in Limited Editions](https://www.earthbox.in/blog/limited-editions-philosophy): Limited editions ensure each piece receives full attention during production. Fifty units per design means we can hand-finish every piece. When editions close, we move to new forms—keeping the catalog fresh and each piece meaningful.
- [The Specimen Card: Documenting Each Piece](https://www.earthbox.in/blog/specimen-card-documentation): The specimen card is a paper record shipped with each piece. It includes edition number, production date, materials used, and care instructions. Signed by the maker, it serves as provenance documentation.
- [Designing for Decades: Timeless Objects](https://www.earthbox.in/blog/designing-for-decades): We avoid trend-driven forms and colors. Neutral palettes age gracefully. Geometric simplicity remains relevant. We test designs against old photographs—if a form would look dated in images from the 1960s, we reconsider.
- [Understanding Light: A Beginner's Guide](https://www.earthbox.in/blog/understanding-light-guide): It depends on the plant. Low-light plants (pothos, snake plant) need 50-250 foot-candles—north-facing windows or room interiors. Medium-light plants need 250-1000 foot-candles—east windows. High-light plants need 1000+ foot-candles—south or west windows.
- [The Right Soil for Terrariums](https://www.earthbox.in/blog/terrarium-soil-guide): Mix 2 parts coco coir, 1 part perlite, 1 part finely chopped orchid bark and ½ part worm castings, over a drainage layer. A thin layer of activated charcoal may help absorb odours. Avoid garden soil—it compacts and may carry pests—and don't use plain potting mix on its own, which holds too much water.
- [Reading Your Plants: Signs of Health and Stress](https://www.earthbox.in/blog/reading-plant-health-signs): Yellow leaves often mean overwatering. Brown crispy edges indicate underwatering or low humidity. Pale leaves suggest insufficient light. Drooping can mean either too much or too little water—check soil moisture to distinguish.
- [Choosing Your First Terrarium Plant](https://www.earthbox.in/blog/choosing-first-terrarium-plant): Fittonia (nerve plant) is ideal—it droops dramatically when thirsty but recovers quickly, teaching you to read water needs. Moss is nearly indestructible. Peperomia tolerates variable conditions. Avoid ferns for first attempts—they are less forgiving.
- [Moss Pole Guide: Supporting Climbing Plants in Mumbai](https://www.earthbox.in/blog/moss-pole-guide-monstera): Yes, Monstera deliciosa naturally climbs trees in the wild. A moss pole mimics this support, encouraging larger leaves, stronger stems, and healthier aerial root development. Without support, Monstera grows horizontally and produces smaller leaves.
- [Stackable Planters: Vertical Gardening for Mumbai Balconies](https://www.earthbox.in/blog/stackable-planters-balcony-garden): Stackable planters are modular units that connect vertically and horizontally. Each block has drainage that flows to the unit below, creating an efficient watering system. You can expand upward or sideways as your collection grows.
- [Plant Care Tags: Never Forget Watering Again](https://www.earthbox.in/blog/plant-care-tags-organization): Care tags use visual symbols to indicate each plant's sunlight and watering needs. A filled sun icon means direct light; half-filled means indirect. Water droplets show frequency—more drops mean more water. At a glance, you know exactly what each plant needs.
